title: Vayishlach: back to Bethel (Genesis 35:1–15)
hookLine: Jacob buries the old idols and returns to where he dreamed

lines: THE HOUSE YOU GREW UP IN.
cards: Maybe you've driven past the house you grew up in. Or walked into the old school gym, or the hospital chapel where you once made a promise. The place looks smaller.
You're older. And you remember who you were, and what you said you'd do. Jacob has met Esau; they've embraced and gone their separate ways.
His family has been through a violent, painful chapter in the town of Shechem. Now God speaks: go up to Bethel. The place of the ladder.

teach.b: Go up to Bethel, God says, live there, and make an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother. Remember that night? The stone for a pillow, the ladder, the vow.
First he turns to his household and says, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "Put away the strange gods that are among you." Purify yourselves, change your clothes. Wait.
Strange gods, in Jacob's camp? The Torah has been hinting. When the family left Laban's house, Rachel secretly took her father's household idols.
After Shechem there was plunder, too. Somewhere in those tents and saddlebags, the old gods came along.
So the family hands them over, the idols and the earrings they wore, and Jacob buries them under the great tree near Shechem. He doesn't smash them in public. He buries them, and leaves them behind.

Then they go up. Along the way Deborah, Rebekah's old nurse, dies, and they bury her under an oak they name the oak of weeping. At Bethel, God appears again, blesses Jacob, and repeats his new name: Israel.
And Jacob does exactly what he did twenty years before: he sets up a stone pillar and pours oil on it.

teach.h: THE SAME STONE, A DIFFERENT MAN.
teach.b: Same place, same stone ritual, different man. The rabbis read Bethel as the promise kept. Jacob vowed there, if God would bring him home in peace.
Now he's back, keeping his side.
But first, he had to bury what he'd been carrying that didn't belong.

how: Jewish tradition treats fulfilling vows seriously, and on Yom Kippur eve the Kol Nidre service opens by addressing unfulfilled vows; Jacob's return to Bethel is read in Vayishlach each late autumn.

o: and he buried, the old gods under a tree
and he sent: the portion that brings Jacob home
and he returned, to Bethel where he dreamed

games.q: what's inside the return — tap the pairs.
p: Rebekah's nurse, by the oak of weeping

s: Jacob smashed the idols in public
he took them, with the earrings, and buried them under the tree near Shechem.
the idols in the camp may go back to Rachel
she had secretly taken her father's household idols when they left Laban.
Jacob set up a stone pillar at Bethel only once
he did it twenty years apart, the night of the ladder and on his return.

games.q: God tells you to go back to Bethel, where you made a vow. you're Jacob. what do you do before you leave?
o: tell everyone to put away the strange gods.
games.why: Jacob told his household to put away the strange gods, purify and change clothes, and he buried the idols under a tree.

practice: Remember a place where you once made a promise, to yourself, to someone you love, or, if you pray, to God, and see it clearly.
Ask what you've picked up since then that doesn't belong on the way back: an old habit, a grudge, something you worship that isn't worth it. Picture burying it under a tree, and walking on.

wordCard.voice: Vayishlach. And he sent: the portion where Jacob buries the old gods under a tree and goes back up to Bethel, where he dreamed.

orig.note: Hebrew: house of God. the place of the ladder, and of Jacob's return.

carryVoice: Your line: bury the old gods. The way back starts with a shovel. That's day one hundred ninety-nine.

sources.q: Put away the strange gods that are among you
